set.n: Fred Noyes' buried gold, his former farm in Eden Township near Scottville
set.pl: Sec. 5 T17N R16W, Eden Township (Mason Co.), near Scottville: the Noyes farm on the 1904 Standard Atlas patrons list (section centroid, provisional)
set.st: Nov 1935: Fred Noyes of Ludington said gold he had buried about 30 years earlier was still on his former farm in Eden Township near Scottville, by then owned by another family; AP put it at $85,000, other copies at $25,000. He had lost the map, and the rail fence and house used as landmarks were gone. He got a federal search warrant (gold-coin ban) and dug with a federal agent; a day's digging failed. The 1904 Mason County atlas lists a Noyes farm in sec. 5, Eden Township (settled 1880). Pin is the section centre, not the spot itself.
set.t: Provisional: the section centre of the 1904 Noyes farm. Look for the old house site and fence lines on the 1938 aerial; a quarter-level fix may follow. Access: private: permission.

tw-mi-north-muskegon-chilson-gold.st: Local papers of June 1897 report his house was moved for the new county gravel road joined to the Whitehall Road; his estate came to $119.83 with no bank deposits, and the gold was never found.
src: Muskegon Chronicle, 16 Jun 1897, p. 7 (newspapers.com 1173865067) and 22 Jun 1897, p. 7 (1173865228)
